title: God's Eye View: A Spy Satellite in Your Browser
description:
God's Eye View turns your browser into a spy satellite, except the data is real: every plane in the sky, every satellite overhead and ships at sea on a live 3D globe. It's free and open source (MIT), it hit #1 on GitHub Trending, and it's past 50,000 stars.

What's on the globe
• 11,000+ live aircraft from public flight trackers (OpenSky, adsb.lol), with military flights on their own layer.
• Ships from AIS, the radio beacons vessels broadcast (AISStream, free key).
• An 838-satellite catalog from CelesTrak, each moved along its orbit with SGP4.
• Earthquakes from the last 24 hours (USGS), active fires (NASA FIRMS), rain radar, lightning, cyclones and wind (NOAA).
• About 3,900 public traffic cameras from city and transport departments (Texas, California, London, Ontario, Finland and more).
• Sensor styles: night vision, FLIR thermal, CRT, Noir and Snow.
• Photorealistic 3D cities from Google's map tiles (via Cesium), and voice control with your own OpenAI key.

Run it
17 of its 20 layers work without an API key. Clone the repo, npm ci, npm run dev, and open localhost:4173 (Node 24). There's also a one-click Pinokio launcher.

The catch
Its own warning: the data may be delayed, incomplete, modeled, inferred or wrong, so it's not for navigation, emergencies or other safety-critical use. Traffic is simulated, camera poses are estimates, and the photorealistic 3D cities need a key (Cesium ion is free for personal use; Google's own key is metered). By design, it doesn't do face recognition or track individual people.
